models.fields: child_all_count (Integer, Indirect Subordinates Count), child_count (Integer, Direct Subordinates Count), department_color (Integer related department_id.color), subordinate_ids (One2many hr.employee, direct+indirect), is_subordinate (Boolean, searchable)

child_all_count (Integer computed from employee), child_count (Integer computed), department_color (Integer computed), subordinate_ids (related employee_id.subordinate_ids), is_subordinate (related employee_id.is_subordinate)

behavioral_notes.observation: _get_subordinates recursively walks child_ids to collect ALL (direct + indirect) reports, carrying a 'parents' accumulator set so the recursion handles the cyclic case where a manager is also a member of a sub-department managed by their own report (e.g. CEO is everyone's manager but sits in an R&D dept under the CTO) — such a manager is excluded from their own subordinate set to avoid infinite recursion. _compute_subordinates then sets subordinate_ids and child_all_count = len(subordinate_ids). All compute methods use compute_sudo=True so subordinate counts are visible even when the current user cannot read individual employee records.

child_count (Direct Subordinates Count) is computed via a single _read_group on parent_id over self.ids (one batched query, not per-record), giving direct-report counts; child_all_count (Indirect Subordinates Count) is a recursive=True field equal to the size of the full subordinate_ids closure. The two integers feed the 'X direct / Y indirect' badges the org-chart widget shows on each node.

get_org_chart loads the employee as hr.employee.public (with has_access('read') gating), then walks parent_id upward in a while-loop bounded by _managers_level=5 (+1) to build the 'ancestors' manager chain, breaking on self-cycles and already-seen ancestors; it returns {self, managers (reversed, capped, plus managers_more flag), children}. Each node is shaped by _prepare_employee_data which exposes id, name, job, a /mail/view redirect link, direct_sub_count (len(child_ids - self)) and indirect_sub_count (child_all_count). get_subordinates returns direct, indirect, or all subordinate ids for the 'see all subordinates' drill-down. get_redirect_model returns 'hr.employee' or 'hr.employee.public' depending on read access, so the widget redirects to the model the user is allowed to open.

behavioral_notes.element: parent_id / child_ids hierarchy reuse + web_hierarchy dependency
behavioral_notes.observation: The module defines NO new business model (0 _name); it only _inherits hr.employee and hr.employee.public to add org-chart compute fields and reuses the existing parent_id (manager) / child_ids self-relation from hr as the hierarchy backbone. It depends on web_hierarchy and registers a hierarchy view (hr_employee_hierarchy) plus an employee-form field widget, auto-installing whenever hr is present.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (OWL/JS) — the org chart IS a client-side OWL component (gap #3)
behavioral_notes.observation: The org chart itself is rendered entirely client-side: OWL components HrOrgChart (the 'hr_org_chart' field widget on the employee form) and HrOrgChartPopover (per-node hover popover) under static/src/fields, plus a custom hr_employee_hierarchy view (card + renderer) under static/src/views. HrOrgChart uses useRecordObserver to refetch when the record's parent_id/resId changes and calls the /hr/get_org_chart RPC to populate managers/self/children; node clicks call get_formview_action to redirect to the employee form. None of this rendering/interaction logic is visible in Python metadata — it lives only in the JS/XML assets (gap #3).

it_architecture.application: hr_org_chart (Org-chart widget extension of the Employees application; auto-installed with hr)
logical_data_erm: hr.employee -> hr.employee (parent_id manager, reused from hr)
hr.employee -> hr.employee (child_ids direct reports, reused from hr)
hr.employee.public -> hr.employee (employee_id; mirrors the same org-chart fields)
information_flows: read-flow: OWL HrOrgChart widget -> /hr/get_org_chart RPC -> walks parent_id chain + child_ids -> returns managers/self/children
access-flow: /hr/get_redirect_model -> picks hr.employee vs hr.employee.public per read access; compute_sudo exposes counts without exposing records
no side-effects: read-only visualization; no records created/written, no external HTTP/SDK calls

capabilities: Visualize Employee Reporting Hierarchy (managers up / subordinates down)
Navigate the Org Chart (drill into managers, peers, subordinates)
Access-aware Org Visualization (public vs private employee model)
policies: compute_sudo=True on org-chart fields: subordinate counts computed bypassing per-record ACLs
controller gates each node on hr.employee.public.has_access('read') and redirects to the readable model via /hr/get_redirect_model
manager-chain walk capped at _managers_level=5 with cycle-breaking on recursive hierarchies

Manager (viewing their reporting line and team)

classification.rationale: hr_org_chart is firm-infrastructure / HR support: an org-visualization widget bolted onto the employee record. Under Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a support value configuration, not a primary chain/shop/network flow — it converts no demand into product and owns no business object of its own (0 new models; it only inherits hr.employee/hr.employee.public to add computed hierarchy fields). It belongs to APQC PCF category 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital, specifically organization-structure management and workforce visualization (reporting-line / span-of-control display). It auto-installs with hr and exists purely to make the existing parent_id/child_ids manager hierarchy navigable.

standard_capabilities: Interactive org-chart widget on the employee form (managers above, direct reports below, hover popover per node)
Direct and indirect (recursive) subordinate counts per employee
Dedicated hr_employee_hierarchy view (web_hierarchy) for browsing the whole tree
Access-aware rendering: routes through hr.employee.public and redirects to whichever model the user may read
Cycle-safe recursion handling managers who are also members of their own sub-departments
typical_fits: Show an employee their reporting line and team on the standard employee form
Let HR explore span of control / department structure without custom reporting
Auto-enable org charts on any database that has the Employees app
common_gaps: No headcount/FTE roll-up analytics on the chart itself
No printable/exportable org-chart document out of the box
Manager-chain depth fixed at _managers_level=5 (code constant, not configurable per company)
